claims.reason: Garner, Popular Electronics July 1971 pp. 79–80 describes the 96-element/288-electrode line scanner and mechanical second axis; Tompsett et al., Charge-Coupled Imaging Devices: Experimental Results, November 1971 pp. 992–995 and figures 4–5 report actual reproduction of text and grayscale photograph; Boornard p. 46 independently describes this array. July dates the report, not a precise invention date. It is distinct from the existing Fairchild 500-element product.

Boyle and Smith, Charge Coupled Semiconductor Devices (1970), p. 592 proposes charge storage/readout and optical use; Tompsett et al. 1971 pp. 992–995 reports this imager; independent RCA engineer Boornard 1972 pp. 45–46 cites both and identifies original structure and later working array. The link is directed from the imager to the concept.

claims.path: bell-labs-buried-channel-ccd identity, description, organization and events
claims.reason: Krambeck US 3,739,240 front page and figure 5 document a Bell Labs filing dated 6 April 1971 describing subsurface charge; Walden et al. The Buried Channel Charge Coupled Device (1972), pp. 1638–1639, report conductance tests and explicitly state those structures failed as CCDs. The event preserves the failure qualification.

Krambeck background and Walden et al. 1972 pp. 1635–1636 cite original surface CCD and explain the buried design; independent Fairchild investigator Kim, Design and Operation of Buried Channel CCDs (1973), pp. 7–10, compares surface and subsurface mechanisms and reports device behavior. Relation is design adaptation, not a claim of prior working CCD operation.

claims.path: charge-coupled-image-sensor identity, description, earliest_record, events and existing facets
claims.reason: Electronics 22 May 1972 pp. 29–31 reports a Fairchild Palo Alto 500-element buried-channel device; Electronics 15 February 1973 p. 31 references that device as a test bed; 29 March 1973 p. 25 explicitly cross-references the February report for the planned first 500-element product. Fairchild CCD101 advertisement 24 May 1973 pp. 43–45 supports named offer and architecture. The broadened record distinguishes prototype and named commercial offer, and does not assert unchanged specimen identity.

Early oral history 1999, buried channel section and preceding exchange, recalls Bell discussion and visit, and recruitment of Amelio; Smith oral history 17 January 2001, Bell stops CCD research, independently recalls Amelio’s early Bell experiment and Fairchild role; Electronics May 1972 p.29 describes Fairchild clocked transfer. This supports general CCD concept uptake, not a specific buried-channel transfer.

Walden et al. 1972 pp. 1635–1636 describes Bell subsurface charge storage and Kim 1973 pp. 7–10 independently describes Fairchild subsurface storage; CCD101 advertisement pp. 43–45 describes the buried channel. The affinity claim is architectural, not a transmission claim; Early’s account and caveat preserve uncertainty about direct transfer.
